data.title: Chevrolet May Cut 2027 Bolt Production Even Lower than Expected
data.description:
If you’re interested in the limited-production Chevrolet Bolt, you may need to rush to secure your vehicle.  

According to United Auto Workers (UAW) documents released to the media, Chevrolet appears to be significantly lowering its target production numbers for their entry-level EV. When it was originally announced, Chevrolet confirmed that the 2027 Chevrolet Bolt would be a limited production run of 150,000 vehicles from its Fairfax plant.

￼However, these new documents show the target is less than a quarter of that, with only 35,000 2027 Bolts expected to come off the production line.

Chevy spokespeople did not confirm the report, but noted they do not publicly verify target numbers, nor did they appear to reconfirm the original 150,000 production number.

Now, a North American major automaker not following through on a limited-run production forecast is nothing new. Ford did it back in the mid-2000s with the Thunderbird, while other launches have exceeded production targets like the Ford GT (Second Edition) and Porsche 911 R and GT3.

The specific reason for potentially limiting an already limited run will become clear over the next few months. Many in the auto industry point to potentially tapering demand in the affordable EV space, while others point to the Trump Administration’s changes to fuel-economy targets as the reason for the drop.

Whatever the reason, if you want a 2027 Bolt, you’ll need to move fast and consider pre-ordering at your local Chevrolet dealership.

data.title: GM’s U.S. EV Sales Plunge 61.7% in Q3 2026
data.description:
General Motors (GM) saw its electric vehicle sales fall sharply in the United States during the third quarter of 2026, with several of its highest-volume EVs posting declines of more than 50%.

According to GM’s Q3 2026 report, the automaker delivered 25,473 EVs during the three-month period, down 61.7% from its record 66,501 deliveries during the same period last year – a decline of 41,028 vehicles.

That drop meant EVs accounted for just 3.8% of GM’s 670,974 total U.S. deliveries during the quarter, compared with 9.4% a year ago. Overall GM sales fell 5.5%, with the company pointing to “the much smaller EV market and discontinued vehicles” as contributing factors.

Q3 was also GM’s weakest EV quarter so far this year. The company sold 25,851 EVs in Q1 and 30,828 in Q2. Through the first nine months of 2026, GM has delivered 82,152 EVs, down 43.2% from 144,668 during the same period last year.

Cadillac was the standout within GM’s EV portfolio. Its four electric models — Lyriq, Optiq, Vistiq and Escalade IQ/IQL — combined for 12,358 deliveries, representing nearly half of GM’s EV volume and 38.0% of Cadillac’s 32,560 total sales.

The Cadillac Optiq was GM’s best-selling EV with 4,550 deliveries, down just 6.9% from 4,886 last year. The returning Chevrolet Bolt ranked second with 3,866 sales, followed by the Lyriq at 3,617, down 50.5%. Escalade IQ/IQL sales declined 29.2% to 1,604. GM also says Cadillac expanded its lead in the luxury EV market by 1.3 percentage points year-to-date through August.

The biggest decline came from the Chevrolet Equinox EV. Once GM’s best-selling electric vehicle, Equinox EV sales collapsed 92.4% compared with Q3 2025.

Elsewhere, the Blazer EV fell 84.4% to 1,261 units, while Silverado EV sales dropped 58.0% to 1,655. GMC’s Hummer EV declined 72.9% to 1,423, and Sierra EV sales were down 50.8% to 1,661.

In Canada, the picture had been different earlier this year. GM Canada reported EV sales were up 33.4% through the first half of 2026, although the company has not yet released Canadian Q3 figures.

GM wasn’t the only U.S. automaker to see lagging EV sales. Ford also reported a steep decline, down 80% compared to a year ago.

data.title: Ford EV Sales Sink 80% in Q3 as Mach-E and Lightning Struggle
data.description:
Ford’s electric vehicle sales continued to slide in the third quarter of 2026, falling 80% compared to a record-setting quarter a year ago, with all three of its remaining EVs posting significant declines.

According to Ford’s U.S. sales tables, the automaker sold just 6,047 EVs during the quarter, down 80.2% from 30,612 in Q3 2025 and 38.0% from the 9,746 delivered in Q2 2026.

Last year’s comparison was unusually strong, as buyers rushed to take advantage of the US$7,500 federal EV tax credit before it expired on September 30, 2025. However, the continued quarter-over-quarter decline shows Ford’s EV slowdown extends beyond that one-time effect.

EVs accounted for only 1.2% of Ford’s U.S. sales during Q3, compared with 5.6% one year earlier.

The Mustang Mach-E remained Ford’s top-selling EV with 5,574 units, but that was down 72.4% from its record 20,177 sales in Q3 2025. Mach-E sales also dropped 20.7% from 7,032 in the second quarter.

The F-150 Lightning recorded an even steeper decline. Ford sold just 289 units, down 97.1% from 10,005 a year ago and 2,421 in Q2. Ford ended production of the battery-electric Lightning in late 2025 as it prepares an extended-range electric successor.

E-Transit sales dropped 57.2% to 184 units from 430 last year.

Through September, Ford has sold 22,653 EVs in the U.S., down 67.5% from 69,600 during the same period in 2025.

Hybrids performed considerably better, although sales still declined 19.7% to 44,308. Combined EV and hybrid sales totaled 50,355, down 41.3%. One bright spot was the Maverick Hybrid, which jumped 59.6% to a third-quarter record of 27,793 units.

Across its entire lineup, Ford sold 509,764 vehicles in Q3, down 6.6% year-over-year and about 7.2% from 549,200 in Q2. Year-to-date sales stand at 1,516,279, down 8.6%.

Ford’s next major EV launch is the Fathom midsize pickup, scheduled to arrive in early 2027 starting at US$28,350. In Canada, the Fathom will start at C$42,690 before the EVAP rebate, with pre-orders opening in early 2027.

data.title: Aston Martin Pushes First Electric Vehicle to 2033, Citing Fast Changing Legislation
data.description:
Luxury automaker Aston Martin has once again postponed its first EV, this time to 2033. The company blames the delay on unpredictable legislation.

Aston Martin fans who want to drive an EV from the brand will have to wait a bit more. According to the CEO Adrian Hallmark, the latest tentative release date is now 2033. He revealed this at a media event in London.

The automakerinitially targeted 2025, but pushed it to 2027. Even under a new management team, the elusive electric car got postponed to 2030, before the latest delay to 2033.

Hallmark cited EV legislation as the culprit. He stated that policies change faster than automakers can cope with. The boss also implied that Aston Martin is sceptical of demand for top-end EVs. Cooling demand in the higher-cost bracket is common concern in the EV sector, with Tesla recently ending production of its two most expensive models.

Meanwhile, Aston Martin customers may be even more disappointed that 2033 is not a firm date. According to Hallmark, “I’m not going to give an absolute date, because it’s imprecise. It could be 2035, it might be 2033, but it’s in that three-year window. It’s not 2031.” (via Autocar)

For now, Aston Martin will focus on traditional internal combustion engines that it is known for. The company, however, recognises the need to comply with EV legislation by 2035 and plans to be ready for it.

Before the 2035 deadline, Aston Martin will likely be silently developing an electric model based on EV technologies from other automakers such as Lucid and Mercedes-Benz.

data.title: Quebec’s Provincial Election Could Change the EV Landscape in the Province
data.description:
As Quebecers head to the polls next week, the EV landscape in la belle province could dramatically shift overnight.

AVEQ and Electric Mobility Canada examined the major parties’ campaign promises and reached out to parties whose platforms were silent on key EV questions.

The result is mixed, but four of the five parties generally support continuing the province’s zero-emission vehicle programs.

data.title: Tesla adds 15,000 Supercharger stalls in 15 months
data.description:
Tesla’s Supercharger network has passed another milestone, with more than 85,000 charging stalls now spread across over 9,000 sites worldwide. The latest update comes only six months after the company celebrated its 80,000th stall in France.

Tesla Charging announced the new totals on Friday, offering a fresh snapshot of the network’s growing footprint. While stalls represent individual charging spaces, sites refer to the locations where those chargers are installed.

When we reported the 80,000 stall milestone in April, Tesla had expanded its Saint-Saturnin station near Le Mans to 48 stalls. That project also included solar canopies and restroom facilities. Today, the 85,000th stall is located in Tsuchiura, Japan.

Comparing the two milestones puts the increase at roughly 5,000 stalls in just under six months.

Zooming further out and we can see how much the network has grown. Tesla reached 60,000 stalls in October 2024 and 70,000 in June 2025. It has now moved another 15,000 stalls in just 15 months, or the equivalent of about 1,000 stalls added every month.

The expansion comes as demand for Supercharging continues to rise. In a separate quarterly update released earlier this week, Tesla reported 69 million charging sessions during Q3 2026, an increase of 29% year over year. Since its launch, Tesla’s Supercharger network has supplied 28.9 terawatt-hours (TWh) of electricity to EVs. That’s equivalent to roughly 482 million full charges of a 60 kWh battery.

To speed up growth, Tesla is also simplifying construction with factory-assembled designs that reduce the work needed on-site. Its Folding Unit Superchargers combine a V4 cabinet and eight charging stalls in one package, allowing 16 stalls to travel on a single truck.

The newer Accordion Supercharger adapts that approach for chargers positioned between parking spaces, expanding into place after delivery.

data.title: Starlink Mini drops to $199 in Canada, $149 in the U.S.
data.description:
SpaceX has lowered the Starlink Mini price to $199 in Canada, making its portable satellite internet kit considerably cheaper than when it first arrived here. South of the border, the price has also been reduced to $149, down from $199.

For Canadians, the latest price is half the $399 introductory offer available when the Mini launched in December 2024.

But that special offer didn’t stay for long. By the spring, the Mini had increased in price to $599, with a several temporary promotions through the year bringing it back to $399.

Prices moved lower again towards the end of the year, when the Canadian kit dropped to $299. In January 2026, SpaceX reduced it to $279.

Today’s $199 price is $80 below that January offer, a further reduction of about 29%.

While SpaceX hasn’t provided a reason for the latest price cut, it could be clearing the way for the reported Starlink Mini 2, which is expected to feature a built-in battery. Details around the next-generation antenna were revealed in June.

The existing Starlink Mini combines the satellite dish and Wi-Fi router in one backpack-sized unit. The dish weighs about 1.1 kg and typically draws 25–40 watts, making it practical for camping, RV trips or working somewhere without cellular coverage.

It can also run from a compatible external battery with the appropriate cable, although it still needs a clear view of the sky to maintain a reliable connection.

Related Articles:

data.title: Geely Rolls Out 2.25 MW EV Chargers in China with sub-Nine-Minute Charging
data.description:
Geely has started rolling out its new Smart Charging C12 stations in China, bringing a peak charging output of 2.25 MW (2,250 kW) per connector to several major cities.

According to Chinese media reports, the new chargers are already installed in Hangzhou, Shanghai, Ningbo, Jiaxing and Xi’an. Geely unveiled the fifth-generation charging system in Ningbo on September 23.

While the 2,250 kW is impressive, it is the charger’s peak output rather than what current vehicles can accept. CarNewsChina reports that the compatible Zeekr 001 and Lynk & Co 10 currently top out at around 1,100 kW.

Still, paired with Geely’s new 12C Shendun Golden Battery, the charging times are extremely quick. In Geely’s tests, the two models charged from 10 to 70 per cent in 4 minutes and 30 seconds, and from 10 to 97 per cent in just 8 minutes and 40 seconds.

Geely says its Xingrui PowerMind AI system predicts battery temperature up to 30 seconds in advance and adjusts charging power, while an end-to-end liquid cooling system helps manage temperatures throughout the charging process.

The rollout adds another player to China’s rapidly growing megawatt charging race. BYD’s megawatt Flash Charging system peaks at 1,500 kW per connector, with the automaker having already deployed more than 10,000 Flash Charging stations across China, with a goal to reach 20,000 by year-end.

Geely hasn’t announced any Canadian charging plans for the technology, though it has been hiring in Toronto as it prepares for a Canadian launch. The company has also recently expanded its charging interests through a battery-swapping deal with NIO Power.

data.title: Rivian Beats Wall Street Estimates With Record Q3 2026 Deliveries
data.description:
Rivian set a new quarterly delivery record in Q3 2026, beating Wall Street expectations as the EV maker continues to ramp production of the new R2.

The company announced on Friday that it delivered 19,248 vehicles during the three months ending September 30, comfortably ahead of the roughly 18,000 deliveries analysts were expecting.

Deliveries were also up sharply from earlier this year. Rivian handed over 12,194 vehicles in Q2, meaning deliveries jumped 57.8% quarter-over-quarter. Compared with the 13,201 vehicles delivered in Q3 2025, the latest figure represents a 45.8% increase.

Production followed a similar trajectory. Rivian built 19,751 vehicles during the quarter, up from 12,613 in Q2. All of those vehicles were produced at the company’s lone manufacturing facility in Normal, Illinois.

The 19,248 deliveries also set a new quarterly record for Rivian. The previous high was 15,564 vehicles in Q3 2023.

The major reason for the boost in both production and deliveries is the arrival of the R2. Customer deliveries of Rivian’s smaller and less expensive SUV began in June, making Q3 the first full quarter with R2 deliveries included in the totals.

Rivian does not provide a model-by-model breakdown, so it is unclear how many of the quarter’s deliveries were R2s. The company is currently selling only the higher-priced R2 Performance through the end of 2026 as it ramps production.

That ramp is still evolving. Rivian previously said it expected to scale R2 production to two shifts by the end of Q3, although the company had not announced the start of that second shift as of Friday morning. Rivian has also pushed customer availability of the R2’s LiDAR hardware to 2027.

Rivian reaffirmed its full-year guidance of 65,000 to 70,000 deliveries, a range it raised in July from 62,000 to 67,000. Rivian said its Q3 production and delivery results were in line with its outlook.

With 41,807 vehicles delivered through the first nine months, Rivian needs at least 23,193 deliveries in Q4 to reach the bottom of its guidance, or 28,193 to reach the top

Rivian will report its full Q3 financial results on Thursday, October 29, after the market closes.

data.title: Get Paid To Charge at Home: Compare EV Charging Rewards Program in Canada
data.description:
EV charging rewards programs are becoming more common in Canada, giving drivers more ways to earn money from charging at home. But with new operators entering the market all the time, knowing which is the best program beyond simply the advertised rate can be difficult.

To help, we’ve launched a new EV charging rewards page that brings 20 programs together in one place.

The page compares programs that share Clean Fuel Regulations credit revenue with drivers. Each listing explains who runs the program, which hardware it supports, how and when you get paid, and how to sign up.

For Tesla owners, a dedicated filter makes it easier to find compatible options. WattsApp, RoadToEV and Roulez Électrique Club accept the Tesla Wall Connector, while most other programs require an OCPP-compatible charger. You can also filter the listings by province and charger type.

A built-in earnings estimator helps you compare potential annual payouts. It defaults to 3,500 kWh of home charging per year, but you can adjust that figure using a slider or enter your own usage. Estimates use each program’s highest advertised rate, so your actual earnings may be lower.

Before enrolling, there are a few details to check beyond the advertised rate. Many programs pay only once a year, and their payout schedules and exit terms vary.

One of the most important rules to understand before switching providers is that a charger can only be enrolled in one program per calendar year. If you’re already enrolled, signing up with another provider in the same year could disqualify your charger from both programs, leaving you without a payout.

If you plan to switch, you need to leave your current program before December 31 and join the new one on or after January 1. Check the operator’s exit terms in advance so you know what is required.

Visit our EV charging rewards page to compare the programs available where you live and see how much your home charging could earn.
